summary: The original 80-ft tower on Rattlesnake Pike in Moshannon State Forest dates to 1933 and was later replaced by a new 80-ft steel structure.

facts.design: 80-ft steel tower with 7 x 7 ft metal cab (original, 1933); replacement is an 80-ft steel structure

events.note: Original 80-ft steel tower built on a rocky ridge in Moshannon State Forest; the state ordered three new 80-ft towers in July 1933
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 155, PA 6
February 2017 visit report: tower still staffed, at least at times

New 80-ft steel structure replaces the original under the late-2010s upgrades. The register gives no exact year; 2018 is inferred from the WHYY report (article dated May 2019 in page metadata) that 16 towers were built statewide the year before its spring fire season. The report does not name this site. Not confirmed for this site.
Original tower removed; its stone observer's cabin remains on site. Year is inferred with the replacement; the register gives none.

corrections.why: The register says the original tower was built in 1933, and a 1933 newspaper item describes the new 80-foot tower on the Rattlesnake Pike. No source read gives 1928.

sources.title: With New Lookout Towers, Pennsylvania Goes Old-School to Detect Wildfires

notes_for_editor: Built year 1933 is supported (register, 1933 press); the record's 1928 is not. Replacement year 2018 is inferred, not confirmed for this site: the register says only late-2010s and the WHYY piece covers statewide towers. The brief's Aermotor design is not supported by any source read, so it is left out of facts. Access and climbing status are not stated in the sources; the register notes directions are signed and a sign reads Rattlesnake Fire Tower. Do not encourage climbing. The WHYY article (datePublished 2019-05-10 in page metadata) does not name the Rattlesnake tower. Thin evidence overall.
